name: Shee Finnaha
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

attributes.attribute: king of the Tuatha Dé Danann
near Newtown Hamilton on the Armagh-Monaghan border

text: Shee Finnaha is an Irish mythological site. It was the palace of Lir, one of the kings of the Tuatha Dé Danann. The people of the Tuatha Dé Danann were the old divine race of Ireland. The palace stood near the town of Newtown Hamilton. The town sits on the border of counties Armagh and Monaghan. Today it lies in Northern Ireland. No ruin marks the spot. The name survives in story as the home of Lir and his fateful children. The same Lir saw his sons and daughter turned to swans, a tale of the Children of Lir. Shee Finnaha keeps that sorrow tied to a place on the map.
